short_description: A teenager with polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis who is experiencing wrist and elbow discomfort, school limitations and reduced dance participation.
referral_reason: Referred by her primary care physician as a cost-effective way to help manage her condition; assess impact of joint symptoms on school and dance activities.

task: Conduct a professional health-promotion interview to understand the patient's concerns, daily activities, participation, goals and relevant health behaviors.

facts.text: Her name is Sofia Hernandez and she is 13 years old, in middle school (grades 6-8).
She has polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), diagnosed when she was 8. It is considered refractory (hard to control).
She takes etanercept and methotrexate for her arthritis.
She has pain and swelling in both elbow joints and her left ankle, and pain and limitation in both wrists.

Her elbows and wrists hurt 4-6 out of 10 at rest every day, rising to 6-8 out of 10 when getting dressed or carrying her backpack. Her left ankle is 2 out of 10 at rest, up to 5 out of 10 with stairs, squatting, or dancing.
She has a cluster of yellow crusted plaques under her nose that is painful and itchy; it's been there 3 days.
She is currently limited in dressing herself, preparing meals, and doing her schoolwork.

Reaching overhead, behind her head, and behind her back are impaired and guarded; grasping and manipulating objects are impaired and provoke pain. Stepping up is impaired - she prefers leading with her right leg.
Getting up from lying provokes elbow and wrist pain; sit-to-stand and squatting provoke left-ankle pain. Walking is not impaired.
She uses some orthotic/assistive or adapted devices, and there are barriers at home (stairs) that limit her getting around independently.
She used to love going to her hip-hop dance class, but is currently limited. She gets about 30-60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity a day and isn't doing organized sports.
She prefers being inside watching TV or listening to hip-hop music. Her favorite shows are 'American Vandal' and 'Friends' re-runs.
She lives in a mobile home with her mom and dad.
She has one close friend she hangs out with outside of school.
Her parents report she is 'not herself' since she can't dance like she used to, and she is starting to isolate herself.
Dance is the thing she loves most; she wants to be able to dance again, dress herself without pain, and keep up with schoolwork.

Her family's medical insurance is inadequate: they meet their deductible every year because of her medication and specialty-care costs, but can't afford the 20% coinsurance for multiple PT visits. They also lack adequate access to transportation and healthcare providers.

Her diet is not well-balanced (short on fruits/vegetables), though she drinks enough fluids and has about 1 sugary drink or juice a day. No special diet. She and family members have had dental cavities.
Family history includes circulation/vascular problems and high blood pressure.
At her annual PT visit: heart rate 70, respiratory rate 14, blood pressure 110/60, oxygen 98%. Height 157 cm, weight 45 kg, BMI 18.1, waist 25 inches.
She walked 400 meters (1312 ft) in the 6-minute walk test. Single-leg stance: eyes open 8 s left / 20 s right; eyes closed 5 s left / 10 s right. Pediatric Balance Scale 30.

Range of motion: both elbows flex to about 110 degrees, wrists move about 40-50 degrees, left ankle dorsiflexion about 10 degrees. Grip strength is impaired, elbow strength significantly reduced, knees and ankle moderately reduced. Muscle tone normal, sensation normal, posture unremarkable, age-appropriate motor development.
Some days at school it's hard to do her schoolwork because of her hands and wrists; carrying her backpack makes the pain worse. She's in regular classes (no special education services).
Her PAVING wellness wheel totals: Physical Activity 24, Stress 10, Variety 12, Energy 21, Nutrition 17, Sleep 25, Attitude 23, Time-outs 17, Investigations 9, Purpose 21, Social 25, Goals 5.
